items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: there was a guy upstairs in London at the studio — I guess at Apple or wherever they were recording and his name was “Harry the Cutter” or he called him “Harry the Cut-ter” and he was the guy who could cut acetates for them.

ctx.x: It did, indeed. Let me ask you about — I got this thought in my head sort of full circle that when you were young you were playing Beatles music and then X number of years later you’re playing with Paul McCartney. Pretty cool.

It is. It was actually pretty cool for Bucky too, which is the funny part. He was so excited. Because I got the call first and I could do literally one day. I flew in from Georgia, did the gig, flew out the next day to a gig in Clarksville, Tennessee and they still had another day. So somewhere before the date they called me and said, “Do you think your father would do the date?” I said, “He’s in the book, I said, “he’ll go anywhere.” So he got there. I was there. I got there at 10 AM. Me and Al Schmidt were the…

lot of fun because you know we did “The Christmas Song” for another record at the same date, “Chestnuts roasting on an open fire” and she was trying to play the intro and she was under the gun ‘cause she was the director. And she’d be like thinking about everything that’s going on. So she was playing and then she finally looked over at me and she goes, “You play the intro.” And I was like okay. And that was like, that’s something we’d talk about, you know, it was Bucky Pizzarelli 101 because every class that I…
